np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    a = np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float64)\n    b = np.asarray(b, dtype=np.float64)\n    if a.size < 2 or np.std(a) == 0 or np.std(b) == 0:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return float(np.corrcoef(a, b)[0, 1])\n\n\ndef _safe_rank(x: np.ndarray, name: str = \"\") -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"scipy.stats.rankdata propagates NaN to the WHOLE output array if a single element is NaN.\n    Every caller here is expected to have already excluded/filled undefined entries; if a stray NaN\n    still shows up, impute with the column median (log it loudly) rather than silently returning an\n    all-NaN rank vector that then cascades into 'point=nan' results downstream.\"\"\"\n    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)\n    bad = np.isnan(x)\n    if bad.any():\n        med = np.nanmedian(x) if not bad.all() else 0.0\n        logger.warning(f\"_safe_rank: {int(bad.sum())}/{len(x)} NaN in '{name}' before ranking -- \"\n                       f\"imputing with the column median ({med}); investigate the upstream mask/fill.\")\n        x = np.where(bad, med, x)\n    return rankdata(x)\n\n\ndef spearman(a: np.ndarray, b: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    a = np.asarray(a, dtype=np.float64)\n    b = np.asarray(b, dtype=np.float64)\n    if a.size < 2:\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return pearson(_safe_rank(a, \"spearman:a\"), _safe_rank(b, \"spearman:b\"))\n\n\ndef ordinal_rank_rows(X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Fast ordinal (no tie-averaging) rank along axis=1; fine for continuous simulated data.\"\"\"\n    return np.argsort(np.argsort(X, axis=1, kind=\"quicksort\"), axis=1).astype(np.float64) + 1.0\n\n\ndef row_pearson(A: np.ndarray, B: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Vectorised Pearson correlation per row of A (n_rows,n) vs B (n_rows,n).\"\"\"\n    Ac = A - A.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    Bc = B - B.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    num = (Ac * Bc).sum(axis=1)\n    den = np.sqrt((Ac ** 2).sum(axis=1) * (Bc ** 2).sum(axis=1))\n    with np.errstate(divide=\"ignore\", invalid=\"ignore\"):\n        out = num / den\n    return out\n\n\ndef safe_log10(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)\n    return np.log10(np.clip(x, 1e-9, None))\n\n\ndef ols_resid_rank(y: np.ndarray, covariate_ranks: list[np.ndarray]) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Rank-transform y, regress its ranks on [1, covariate_ranks...] by OLS, return residuals.\"\"\"\n    ry = _safe_rank(y, \"ols_resid_rank:y\").astype(np.float64)\n    n = len(ry)\n    X = np.column_stack([np.ones(n)] + [_safe_rank(c, \"ols_resid_rank:cov\").astype(np.float64)\n                                        for c in covariate_ranks])\n    try:\n        beta, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(X, ry, rcond=None)\n    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:\n        return np.full(n, np.nan)\n    return ry - X @ beta\n\n\ndef partial_spearman(value: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, covariates: list[np.ndarray]) -> float:\n    rv = ols_resid_rank(value, covariates)\n    rt = ols_resid_rank(target, covariates)\n    if np.any(np.isnan(rv)) or np.any(np.isnan(rt)):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    return pearson(rv, rt)\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# Row loading / joining\n# =================================================================================================\ndef load_rows(rows_glob: str) -> list[dict]:\n    paths = sorted(WS.glob(rows_glob))\n    rows = []\n    for p in paths:\n        try:\n            rows.append(json.loads(p.read_text()))\n        except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError) as e:\n            logger.warning(f\"skip unreadable row {p}: {e}\")\n    logger.info(f\"loaded {len(rows)} row files from {rows_glob}\")\n    return rows\n\n\ndef load_labels() -> dict[str, dict]:\n    return json.loads((WS / \"labels_map.json\").read_text())[\"rows\"]\n\n\ndef joined_frame(rows: list[dict], labels: dict[str, dict]) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"One row per model with label-sourced repo/family/lineage/class/stratum/status/BALANCED/PRODUCT,\n    plus n_params/candidates/etc. from the row file itself.\"\"\"\n    recs = []\n    for row in rows:\n        repo = row.get(\"repo\")\n        lab = labels.get(repo)\n        if lab is None:\n            logger.warning(f\"{repo}: not in labels_map.json -- falling back to the row's own copy\")\n            lab = {\"BALANCED\": row.get(\"BALANCED\"), \"PRODUCT\": row.get(\"PRODUCT\"), \"family\": row.get(\"family\"),\n                   \"lineage\": row.get(\"lineage\"), \"class\": row.get(\"class\"), \"stratum\": row.get(\"stratum\"),\n                   \"status\": \"graded\" if row.get(\"graded\") else \"unknown\"}\n        recs.append({\n            \"repo\": repo, \"resolved_sha\": row.get(\"resolved_sha\"),\n            \"family\": lab.get(\"family\"), \"lineage\": lab.get(\"lineage\"), \"class\": lab.get(\"class\"),\n            \"stratum\": lab.get(\"stratum\"), \"label_status\": lab.get(\"status\"),\n            \"BALANCED\": lab.get(\"BALANCED\"), \"PRODUCT\": lab.get(\"PRODUCT\"),\n            \"n_params\": row.get(\"n_params\"), \"row_status\": row.get(\"status\"),\n            \"screen16_file_sha256\": row.get(\"screen16_file_sha256\"), \"prereg_hash\": row.get(\"prereg_hash\"),\n            \"candidate_seconds\": row.get(\"candidate_seconds\", {}), \"candidates\": row.get(\"candidates\", {}),\n            \"oracle\": row.get(\"oracle\", {}), \"offset_control\": row.get(\"offset_control\"),\n            \"C1_linear_range_eps\": row.get(\"C1_linear_range_eps\"),\n            \"C1_linearity\": row.get(\"C1_linearity\"),\n            \"C1_nonlinear_at_primary\": row.get(\"C1_nonlinear_at_primary\"),\n            \"wall_s\": row.get(\"wall_s\"),\n            \"lite\": any(f_.get(\"code\") == \"ANCHOR_LITE\" for f_ in (row.get(\"flags\") or [])),\n        })\n    return pd.DataFrame.from_records(recs)\n\n\ndef graded_mask(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:\n    return (df[\"BALANCED\"].notna()) & (df[\"row_status\"] == \"ok\") & (df[\"stratum\"] == \"chat\")\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# C9 AtP-vs-true-patching validation (PREREG / plan fallback #9)\n# =================================================================================================\ndef assess_c9_atp_reliability(df: pd.DataFrame) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Look up C9.atp_vs_true_pearson on the ATP_VALIDATION_MODELS rows (any status/stratum -- this is\n    a measurement-quality check, not a correlation, so it is read off the full df, before the graded\n    mask). If ANY validation model present has pearson < 0.5, C9 is ATP_UNRELIABLE. If none of the\n    validation models are present with a defined pearson, the row is 'not_verifiable' and AtP is kept\n    (per the fallback plan's own wording).\"\"\"\n    found: dict[str, float] = {}\n    for repo in ATP_VALIDATION_MODELS:\n        hit = df.index[df[\"repo\"] == repo]\n        if len(hit) == 0:\n            continue\n        cd = df.at[hit[0], \"candidates\"] or {}\n        v = (cd.get(\"C9\", {}) or {}).get(\"atp_vs_true_pearson\")\n        if v is not None and math.isfinite(float(v)):\n            found[repo] = float(v)\n    if not found:\n        return {\"status\": \"not_verifiable\", \"atp_unreliable\": False, \"threshold\": ATP_RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD,\n                \"validation_models\": ATP_VALIDATION_MODELS, \"found\": {}, \"triggered\": {},\n                \"reason\": \"no ATP_VALIDATION_MODELS row present with a defined atp_vs_true_pearson; \"\n                          \"AtP is kept (not verifiable)\"}\n    triggered = {r: v for r, v in found.items() if v < ATP_RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD}\n    atp_unreliable = bool(triggered)\n    return {\"status\": \"ATP_UNRELIABLE\" if atp_unreliable else \"verified_reliable\",\n            \"atp_unreliable\": atp_unreliable, \"threshold\": ATP_RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD,\n            \"validation_models\": ATP_VALIDATION_MODELS, \"found\": found, \"triggered\": triggered,\n            \"reason\": (f\"{len(triggered)}/{len(found)} validation model(s) below \"\n                       f\"{ATP_RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD}: {triggered}\" if atp_unreliable else\n                       f\"all {len(found)} validation model(s) >= {ATP_RELIABILITY_THRESHOLD}: {found}\")}\n\n\ndef rewrite_c9_for_atp_unreliable(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"When ATP_UNRELIABLE: true_patch_value becomes C9's PRIMARY value for every model (not just the\n    validation set), and true_patch_pole_refuse/comply/k8 become C9's pole_refuse/pole_comply/k8 for\n    every model. The original AtP numbers are preserved under 'atp'/'atp_pole_refuse'/... (candidate\n    id C9, variant 'atp' in candidate_values_live.json). A model whose true_patch_* field is itself\n    absent (not yet measured / TIME_CAP) is left UNDEFINED for that field rather than falling back\n    silently to AtP, and (for pole_refuse/pole_comply) is recorded in 'c9_true_patch_pole_missing' so\n    s3_check can EXCLUDE it from the pole comparison instead of worst-valuing it (worst-value\n    substitution is a PREREG S1/S3 rule for a measured-but-undefined candidate, not for 'we didn't\n    measure this field under the corrected method yet').\"\"\"\n    df = df.copy()\n    new_cands, missing_flags = [], []\n    for cd in df[\"candidates\"]:\n        cd = dict(cd or {})\n        c9 = dict(cd.get(\"C9\", {}) or {})\n        c9[\"atp_value\"] = c9.get(\"value\")\n        c9[\"atp_undefined\"] = bool(c9.get(\"undefined\", c9.get(\"value\") is None))\n        c9[\"atp_reason\"] = c9.get(\"reason\")\n        tv = c9.get(\"true_patch_value\")\n        if tv is not None:\n            c9[\"value\"], c9[\"undefined\"], c9[\"reason\"] = tv, False, None\n        else:\n            c9[\"value\"], c9[\"undefined\"] = None, True\n            # prefer the model's own true_patch_reason (e.g. TIME_CAP) over a generic message\n            c9[\"reason\"] = c9.get(\"true_patch_reason\") or \\\n                \"ATP_UNRELIABLE: true_patch_value not available for this model\"\n        miss = {}\n        for pv, true_key, reason_key in ((\"pole_refuse\", \"true_patch_pole_refuse\", \"pole_refuse_reason\"),\n                                         (\"pole_comply\", \"true_patch_pole_comply\", \"pole_comply_reason\"),\n                                         (\"k8\", \"true_patch_k8\", \"k8_reason\")):\n            c9[\"atp_\" + pv] = c9.get(pv)\n            tv2 = c9.get(true_key)\n            if tv2 is not None:\n                c9[pv], c9[reason_key] = tv2, None\n            else:\n                c9[pv] = None\n                own_reason = c9.get(true_key + \"_reason\")\n                c9[reason_key] = own_reason or (f\"ATP_UNRELIABLE: {true_key} not available for this \"\n                                                 f\"model (treated as missing, not worst-valued)\")\n                if pv != \"k8\":\n                    miss[pv] = True\n        cd[\"C9\"] = c9\n        new_cands.append(cd)\n        missing_flags.append(miss)\n    df[\"candidates\"] = new_cands\n    df[\"c9_true_patch_pole_missing\"] = missing_flags\n    return df\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# Per-candidate value extraction + worst-value rule\n# =================================================================================================\ndef extract_variant(cdict: dict, variant: str) -> tuple[float | None, bool, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"Return (value, undefined, reason) for one variant of one candidate's dict (already the\n    row[\"candidates\"][cid] sub-dict).\"\"\"\n    if variant == \"primary\":\n        v = cdict.get(\"value\")\n        und = bool(cdict.get(\"undefined\", v is None))\n        return v, und, cdict.get(\"reason\")\n    if variant == \"late\":\n        v = cdict.get(\"late\")\n        return v, v is None, None if v is not None else \"no late-window value\"\n    if variant in (\"pole_refuse\", \"pole_comply\"):\n        v = cdict.get(variant)\n        return v, v is None, cdict.get(variant + \"_reason\")\n    if variant == \"k8\":\n        v = cdict.get(\"k8\")\n        return v, v is None, cdict.get(\"k8_reason\")\n    if variant == \"oracle\":\n        v = cdict.get(\"oracle\")\n        return v, v is None, cdict.get(\"oracle_reason\")\n    if variant == \"null_p95\":\n        v = cdict.get(\"null_p95\")\n        return v, v is None, None if v is not None else \"no direction null defined\"\n    if variant == \"atp\":\n        # C9-only, only meaningful once ATP_UNRELIABLE has swapped 'value' for true_patch_value (see\n        # rewrite_c9_for_atp_unreliable): the original AtP value is preserved here under 'atp_value'.\n        v = cdict.get(\"atp_value\")\n        return v, bool(cdict.get(\"atp_undefined\", v is None)), cdict.get(\"atp_reason\")\n    raise ValueError(variant)\n\n\ndef build_primary_series(df: pd.DataFrame, cid: str) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"DataFrame indexed like df with columns value, undefined, reason for candidate cid's primary value.\"\"\"\n    vals, unds, reas = [], [], []\n    for cd in df[\"candidates\"]:\n        c = (cd or {}).get(cid, {})\n        v, u, r = extract_variant(c, \"primary\")\n        vals.append(v)\n        unds.append(u)\n        reas.append(r)\n    return pd.DataFrame({\"value\": vals, \"undefined\": unds, \"reason\": reas}, index=df.index)\n\n\ndef worst_value(oriented_values: np.ndarray, undefined: np.ndarray) -> float:\n    \"\"\"Worst observed panel value AFTER orientation = the minimum oriented value among defined entries\n    (an oriented candidate is supposed to correlate positively with safety; the worst-looking value is\n    the smallest one).\"\"\"\n    defined = oriented_values[~undefined]\n    if defined.size == 0:\n        return -1e9  # degenerate: everything undefined; use a sentinel that is worse than anything\n    return float(np.min(defined))\n\n\ndef apply_worst_value_rule(raw_values: np.ndarray, undefined: np.ndarray, sign: float | None) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Return ORIENTED values with undefined entries replaced by the panel's worst oriented value.\n    sign=None (two-sided/descriptive candidates) -> no orientation applied (sign=1), no worst-value\n    substitution requested by S1/S3 since these never enter the pass rules; we still fill for safety.\"\"\"\n    s = 1.0 if sign is None else sign\n    oriented = np.array([np.nan if v is None else s * float(v) for v in raw_values], dtype=np.float64)\n    und = np.array(undefined, dtype=bool) | np.isnan(oriented)\n    w = worst_value(oriented, und)\n    out = np.where(und, w, oriented)\n    return out\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# Bootstrap / permutation machinery\n# =================================================================================================\ndef lineage_groups(lineages: np.ndarray) -> dict[Any, np.ndarray]:\n    g = defaultdict(list)\n    for i, lin in enumerate(lineages):\n        g[lin].append(i)\n    return {k: np.array(v) for k, v in g.items()}\n\n\ndef lineage_bootstrap_resample_idx(groups: dict[Any, np.ndarray], rng: np.random.Generator) -> np.ndarray:\n    keys = list(groups.keys())\n    draw = rng.integers(0, len(keys), size=len(keys))\n    return np.concatenate([groups[keys[i]] for i in draw])\n\n\ndef bootstrap_rho_ci(value: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, lineages: np.ndarray, n_boot: int = N_BOOT,\n                     seed: int = SEED, one_sided: bool = False) -> dict:\n    groups = lineage_groups(lineages)\n    if len(groups) < 2:\n        return {\"point\": spearman(value, target), \"ci_lo\": float(\"nan\"), \"ci_hi\": float(\"nan\"),\n                \"n_boot\": 0, \"note\": \"fewer than 2 lineages: bootstrap undefined\"}\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    boots = np.empty(n_boot)\n    ndef = 0\n    for b in range(n_boot):\n        idx = lineage_bootstrap_resample_idx(groups, rng)\n        v, t = value[idx], target[idx]\n        if np.std(v) == 0 or np.std(t) == 0 or len(v) < 3:\n            boots[b] = np.nan\n            continue\n        boots[b] = spearman(v, t)\n        ndef += 1\n    valid = boots[~np.isnan(boots)]\n    point = spearman(value, target)\n    if valid.size == 0:\n        return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo\": float(\"nan\"), \"ci_hi\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_boot\": 0,\n                \"note\": \"all resamples degenerate\"}\n    if one_sided:\n        lo = float(np.percentile(valid, 5))\n        return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo\": lo, \"ci_hi\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_boot\": int(valid.size),\n                \"note\": \"one-sided 95% lower bound (5th pct)\"}\n    lo, hi = np.percentile(valid, [2.5, 97.5])\n    return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo\": float(lo), \"ci_hi\": float(hi), \"n_boot\": int(valid.size), \"note\": None}\n\n\ndef bootstrap_partial_rho_ci(value: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, covariates: list[np.ndarray],\n                             lineages: np.ndarray, n_boot: int = N_BOOT, seed: int = SEED) -> dict:\n    groups = lineage_groups(lineages)\n    point = partial_spearman(value, target, covariates)\n    if len(groups) < 2:\n        return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo_one_sided\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_boot\": 0,\n                \"note\": \"fewer than 2 lineages: bootstrap undefined\"}\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    boots = np.empty(n_boot)\n    for b in range(n_boot):\n        idx = lineage_bootstrap_resample_idx(groups, rng)\n        if len(idx) < len(covariates) + 3:\n            boots[b] = np.nan\n            continue\n        try:\n            boots[b] = partial_spearman(value[idx], target[idx], [c[idx] for c in covariates])\n        except (np.linalg.LinAlgError, ValueError):\n            boots[b] = np.nan\n    valid = boots[~np.isnan(boots)]\n    if valid.size == 0:\n        return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo_one_sided\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_boot\": 0, \"note\": \"all resamples degenerate\"}\n    lo = float(np.percentile(valid, 5))\n    return {\"point\": point, \"ci_lo_one_sided\": lo, \"n_boot\": int(valid.size), \"note\": None}\n\n\ndef checkpoint_perm_null(value: np.ndarray, target: np.ndarray, sign: float, n_perm: int = N_PERM,\n                         seed: int = SEED) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Checkpoint-label permutation null for Spearman(value,target): permute which model each target\n    value is attached to (equivalent to permuting rank(target)); one-sided p in the declared direction.\"\"\"\n    n = len(value)\n    if n < 3 or np.std(value) == 0 or np.std(target) == 0:\n        return {\"observed\": float(\"nan\"), \"p_one_sided\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_perm\": 0}\n    rv = _safe_rank(value, \"checkpoint_perm_null:value\")\n    rt = _safe_rank(target, \"checkpoint_perm_null:target\")\n    observed = pearson(rv, rt)\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    perms = np.array([rng.permutation(n) for _ in range(n_perm)])\n    rt_perm = rt[perms]  # (n_perm, n)\n    rv_c = rv - rv.mean()\n    rt_c = rt_perm - rt_perm.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    num = (rt_c * rv_c).sum(axis=1)\n    den = np.sqrt((rv_c ** 2).sum() * (rt_c ** 2).sum(axis=1))\n    with np.errstate(divide=\"ignore\", invalid=\"ignore\"):\n        null_rho = num / den\n    oriented_obs = sign * observed\n    oriented_null = sign * null_rho\n    p = float(np.mean(oriented_null >= oriented_obs))\n    return {\"observed\": float(observed), \"p_one_sided\": p, \"n_perm\": n_perm}\n\n\ndef direction_null_fraction(raw_values: np.ndarray, null_p95: np.ndarray, undefined: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n    ok = ~undefined & ~np.isnan(null_p95)\n    if ok.sum() == 0:\n        return {\"fraction\": float(\"nan\"), \"n\": 0, \"note\": \"no models with both a value and a null_p95\"}\n    frac = float(np.mean(raw_values[ok] > null_p95[ok]))\n    return {\"fraction\": frac, \"n\": int(ok.sum()), \"note\": None}\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# ICC / MDE / margin power\n# =================================================================================================\ndef icc_oneway(target: np.ndarray, lineages: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n    df = pd.DataFrame({\"t\": target, \"lin\": lineages})\n    groups = df.groupby(\"lin\")[\"t\"]\n    N = len(df)\n    a = groups.ngroups\n    if a < 2 or N <= a:\n        return {\"icc\": 0.0, \"n_lineages\": a, \"mbar\": N / a if a else float(\"nan\"), \"note\": \"degenerate\"}\n    grand = df[\"t\"].mean()\n    SSB = sum(len(g) * (g.mean() - grand) ** 2 for _, g in groups)\n    SSW = sum(((g - g.mean()) ** 2).sum() for _, g in groups)\n    MSB = SSB / (a - 1)\n    MSW = SSW / (N - a)\n    n_i = groups.size().values\n    k0 = (1.0 / (a - 1)) * (N - (n_i ** 2).sum() / N)\n    denom = MSB + (k0 - 1) * MSW\n    icc_raw = (MSB - MSW) / denom if denom != 0 else 0.0\n    icc = float(np.clip(icc_raw, 0.0, 0.95))\n    return {\"icc\": icc, \"icc_raw\": float(icc_raw), \"n_lineages\": int(a), \"mbar\": float(N / a), \"note\": None}\n\n\ndef mde_from_icc(n: int, icc_info: dict) -> dict:\n    mbar = icc_info[\"mbar\"]\n    icc = icc_info[\"icc\"]\n    deff = 1.0 + (mbar - 1.0) * icc\n    n_eff = n / deff if deff > 0 else float(\"nan\")\n    if not np.isfinite(n_eff) or n_eff <= 3:\n        return {\"deff\": deff, \"n_eff\": n_eff, \"mde_rho\": float(\"nan\"), \"note\": \"n_eff <= 3\"}\n    mde_rho = math.tanh((1.645 + 0.842) / math.sqrt(n_eff - 3))\n    return {\"deff\": float(deff), \"n_eff\": float(n_eff), \"mde_rho\": float(mde_rho), \"note\": None}\n\n\ndef margin_power_sim(lineage_sizes: list[int], icc: float, rho_gap_obs: float, margin: float = MARGIN,\n                     n_sims: int = N_SIMS_POWER, n_boot: int = N_BOOT_POWER, seed: int = SEED,\n                     alpha: float = 0.05) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Monte-Carlo power of the |rho_cand|-|rho_gap| >= margin comparison at the realised n/ICC, assuming\n    a candidate whose true (population) |Spearman| with the target exceeds the observed logit-gap\n    Spearman by exactly `margin`. Detection rule mirrors the real S1 rule: a lineage-cluster bootstrap\n    (n_boot resamples, precomputed index sets reused across all simulated worlds for speed) whose\n    one-sided 5th-percentile lower bound of (|rho_cand|-|rho_gap|) is > 0.\"\"\"\n    t0 = time.perf_counter()\n    n_lin = len(lineage_sizes)\n    n = int(sum(lineage_sizes))\n    if n_lin < 2 or n < 4:\n        return {\"power\": float(\"nan\"), \"note\": \"fewer than 2 lineages or n<4: power undefined\"}\n    lineage_of = np.repeat(np.arange(n_lin), lineage_sizes)\n    rho_g = float(np.clip(rho_gap_obs, -0.95, 0.95)) if np.isfinite(rho_gap_obs) else 0.0\n    rho_c = float(np.clip(abs(rho_g) + margin, -0.95, 0.95))\n    icc_c = float(np.clip(icc, 0.0, 0.95))\n    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)\n    u = rng.normal(0.0, math.sqrt(icc_c), size=(n_sims, n_lin))\n    e = rng.normal(0.0, math.sqrt(max(1.0 - icc_c, 1e-6)), size=(n_sims, n))\n    T = u[:, lineage_of] + e\n    epsG = rng.normal(size=(n_sims, n))\n    epsC = rng.normal(size=(n_sims, n))\n    G = rho_g * T + math.sqrt(max(1.0 - rho_g ** 2, 1e-6)) * epsG\n    C = rho_c * T + math.sqrt(max(1.0 - rho_c ** 2, 1e-6)) * epsC\n    lineage_members = [np.where(lineage_of == g)[0] for g in range(n_lin)]\n    rng_b = np.random.default_rng(seed + 1)\n    boot_idx = []\n    for _ in range(n_boot):\n        samp = rng_b.integers(0, n_lin, size=n_lin)\n        boot_idx.append(np.concatenate([lineage_members[g] for g in samp]))\n    diffs = np.empty((n_boot, n_sims))\n    for bi, idx in enumerate(boot_idx):\n        if len(idx) < 4:\n            diffs[bi] = np.nan\n            continue\n        Tb, Cb, Gb = T[:, idx], C[:, idx], G[:, idx]\n        rT, rC, rG = ordinal_rank_rows(Tb), ordinal_rank_rows(Cb), ordinal_rank_rows(Gb)\n        rhoC, rhoG = row_pearson(rT, rC), row_pearson(rT, rG)\n        diffs[bi] = np.abs(rhoC) - np.abs(rhoG)\n    lower = np.nanpercentile(diffs, 5, axis=0)\n    power = float(np.mean(lower > 0))\n    return {\"power\": power, \"rho_gap_assumed\": rho_g, \"rho_cand_assumed\": rho_c, \"n\": n, \"n_lineages\": n_lin,\n            \"n_sims\": n_sims, \"n_boot\": n_boot, \"alpha\": alpha, \"seconds\": round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 2)}\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# LOFO\n# =================================================================================================\ndef lofo_spearman(target: np.ndarray, value: np.ndarray, families: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n    preds = np.full(len(target), np.nan)\n    for fam in np.unique(families):\n        train = families != fam\n        test = families == fam\n        if train.sum() < 2:\n            continue\n        x, y = value[train], target[train]\n        if np.std(x) == 0:\n            preds[test] = y.mean()\n        else:\n            slope, intercept = np.polyfit(x, y, 1)\n            preds[test] = intercept + slope * value[test]\n    ok = ~np.isnan(preds)\n    if ok.sum() < 3:\n        return {\"score\": float(\"nan\"), \"n\": int(ok.sum())}\n    return {\"score\": spearman(target[ok], preds[ok]), \"n\": int(ok.sum())}\n\n\ndef lofo_family_only(target: np.ndarray, families: np.ndarray) -> dict:\n    preds = np.full(len(target), np.nan)\n    for fam in np.unique(families):\n        train = families != fam\n        test = families == fam\n        if train.sum() < 1:\n            continue\n        preds[test] = target[train].mean()\n    ok = ~np.isnan(preds)\n    if ok.sum() < 3:\n        return {\"score\": float(\"nan\"), \"n\": int(ok.sum())}\n    return {\"score\": spearman(target[ok], preds[ok]), \"n\": int(ok.sum())}\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# Per-candidate analysis\n# =================================================================================================\ndef get_raw_series(df: pd.DataFrame, cid: str, variant: str = \"primary\") -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list]:\n    vals, unds, reas = [], [], []\n    for cd in df[\"candidates\"]:\n        c = (cd or {}).get(cid, {})\n        v, u, r = extract_variant(c, variant)\n        vals.append(v)\n        unds.append(u)\n        reas.append(r)\n    raw = np.array([np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in vals], dtype=np.float64)\n    und = np.array(unds, dtype=bool) | np.isnan(raw)\n    return raw, und, reas\n\n\ndef oracle_series(df: pd.DataFrame, base_cid: str) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, list]:\n    vals, unds, reas = [], [], []\n    for cd in df[\"candidates\"]:\n        c = (cd or {}).get(base_cid, {})\n        v = c.get(\"oracle\")\n        r = c.get(\"oracle_reason\")\n        vals.append(v)\n        unds.append(v is None)\n        reas.append(r)\n    raw = np.array([np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in vals], dtype=np.float64)\n    und = np.array(unds, dtype=bool) | np.isnan(raw)\n    return raw, und, reas\n\n\ndef analyse_candidate(cid: str, gdf: pd.DataFrame, to the WHOLE output if a single element is NaN, so the\n    # logit_gap covariate used in every other candidate's partial rho must never contain a NaN:\n    # apply the same worst-value rule used for S1/S3 to it before it is used as a covariate.\n    logit_gap_cov = apply_worst_value_rule(logit_gap_raw, lg_und, ORIENT[\"logit_gap\"])\n\n    if is_oracle:\n        base_cid = cid.replace(\"_oracle\", \"\")\n        raw, und, reasons = oracle_series(gdf, base_cid)\n    else:\n        raw, und, reasons = get_raw_series(gdf, cid, \"primary\")\n    n_undefined = int(und.sum())\n\n    out: dict[str, Any] = {\"definition\": DEFINITION.get(cid, \"\"), \"orientation\": (\"two-sided\" if sign is None\n                           else (\"+\" if sign > 0 else \"-\")), \"role\": role, \"n\": n, \"n_families\": n_families,\n                           \"n_lineages\": n_lineages, \"n_undefined\": n_undefined,\n                           \"undefined_fraction\": n_undefined / n if n else float(\"nan\"),\n                           \"flag_undefined_majority\": bool(n > 0 and n_undefined > n / 2)}\n\n    if n < N_FLOOR:\n        out[\"not_detectable_at_this_n\"] = True\n        out[\"mde\"] = shared_mde\n        out[\"S1\"] = {\"pass\": False, \"reason\": f\"not detectable at this n (n={n} < floor {N_FLOOR}); \"\n                     f\"MDE_rho={shared_mde.get('mde_rho')}\"}\n        for s in (\"S2\", \"S3\", \"S4\", \"S5\", \"S6\"):\n            out[s] = {\"pass\": False, \"reason\": \"not detectable at this n\"}\n        out[\"rho\"] = {}\n        return out\n    out[\"not_detectable_at_this_n\"] = False\n\n    # --- worst-value-substituted oriented series (used ONLY for S1 / S3, per PREREG H5 rule) ---\n    oriented_wv = apply_worst_value_rule(raw, und, sign)\n\n    rho_by_target: dict[str, Any] = {}\n    for tgt_name in TARGETS:\n        tgt = gdf[tgt_name].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n        ok = ~np.isnan(tgt) & ~und\n        rho_ckpt = spearman(raw[ok], tgt[ok]) if ok.sum() >= 3 else float(\"nan\")\n        ci = bootstrap_rho_ci(raw[ok], tgt[ok], lineages[ok]) \\\n            if ok.sum() >= 3 else {\"point\": float(\"nan\"), \"ci_lo\": float(\"nan\"), \"ci_hi\": float(\"nan\"),\n                                    \"n_boot\": 0, \"note\": \"n<3\"}\n        # family means\n        fam_df = pd.DataFrame({\"v\": raw, \"t\": tgt, \"f\": families, \"ok\": ok})\n        fam_df = fam_df[fam_df[\"ok\"]]\n        fam_means = fam_df.groupby(\"f\").agg(v=(\"v\", \"mean\"), t=(\"t\", \"mean\"))\n        rho_family = spearman(fam_means[\"v\"].to_numpy(), fam_means[\"t\"].to_numpy()) if len(fam_means) >= 3 \\\n            else float(\"nan\")\n        rho_by_target[tgt_name] = {\n            \"rho_ckpt\": rho_ckpt, \"rho_ckpt_boot\": ci, \"n_ckpt\": int(ok.sum()),\n            \"rho_family\": rho_family, \"n_families_used\": int(len(fam_means)),\n        }\n    out[\"rho\"] = rho_by_target\n\n    # --- partial rho (BALANCED only, primary) ---\n    tgt = gdf[PRIMARY_TARGET].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n    ok = ~np.isnan(tgt) & ~und\n    ok_wv = ~np.isnan(tgt)  # S1 keeps undefined models at the worst oriented panel value (PREREG H5 rule)\n    if cid == \"logit_gap\":\n        covs = [log_np[ok]]\n        cov_desc = \"log10(n_params) only\"\n    else:\n        covs = bootstrap_partial_rho_ci(oriented_wv[ok_wv], tgt[ok_wv], covs_wv, lineages[ok_wv])\n    elif ok.sum() >= 5:\n        partial_pt = partial_spearman(raw[ok], tgt[ok], covs)\n        boot = targets\";\n    # reported for completeness only -- S1 remains gated on BALANCED alone per PREREG, never on this) ---\n    tgt_p = gdf[\"PRODUCT\"].to_numpy(dtype=np.float64)\n    ok_p = ~np.isnan(tgt_p) & ~und\n    ok_wv_p = ~np.isnan(tgt_p)\n    if ok_wv_p.sum() >= 5 and sign is not None and np.isfinite(oriented_wv[ok_wv_p]).all():\n        covs_wv_p = ([log_np[ok_wv_p]] if cid == \"logit_gap\" else [logit_gap_cov[ok_wv_p], log_np[ok_wv_p]])\n        partial_pt_p = partial_spearman(oriented_wv[ok_wv_p], tgt_p[ok_wv_p], covs_wv_p)\n        boot_p = bootstrap_partial_rho_ci(oriented_wv[ok_wv_p], tgt_p[ok_wv_p], covs_wv_p, lineages[ok_wv_p])\n    elif ok_p.sum() >= 5:\n        covs_p = [log_np[ok_p]] if cid == \"logit_gap\" else [logit_gap_cov[ok_p], log_np[ok_p]]\n        partial_pt_p = partial_spearman(raw[ok_p], tgt_p[ok_p], covs_p)\n        boot_p = bootstrap_partial_rho_ci(raw[ok_p], tgt_p[ok_p], covs_p, lineages[ok_p])\n    else:\n        partial_pt_p, boot_p = float(\"nan\"), {\"point\": float(\"nan\"), \"ci_lo_one_sided\": float(\"nan\"), \"n_boot\": 0}\n    out[\"partial_rho_product\"] = # --- LOFO ---\n    lofo_val = lofo_spearman(tgt[ok], raw[ok], families[ok]) if ok.sum() >= 5 else {\"score\": float(\"nan\"), \"n\": 0}\n    lofo_fam = lofo_family_only(tgt[ok], families[ok]) if out[\"lofo\"] = {\"candidate\": lofo_val, \"family_only\": lofo_fam, \"size_only\": lofo_size}\n\n    # --- MDE / margin (shared panel-level numbers, attached per candidate for convenience) ---\n float(\"nan\")\n    out[\"margin_0.15_over_logit_gap\"] = {\"value\": margin_val, \"descriptive_only\": True,\n                                          \"mde_rho\": shared_mde.get(\"mde_rho\"), \"power_sim\": shared_power}\n\n    # =========================================================== S1..S6\n    S: dict[str, dict] = {}\n    if sign is None:\n        S[\"S1\"] = {\"pass\": False, {role}: never enters S1-S6\"}\n        out[\"S1\"], out[\"S2\"], out[\"S3\"], out[\"S4\"], out[\"S5\"], out[\"S6\"] = (S[\"S1\"], S[\"S2\"], S[\"S3\"], S[\"S4\"],\n s2b_pass = bool(np.isfinite(frac_info[\"fraction\"]) and frac_info[\"fraction\"] >= 0.60)\n        s2_pass = s2a_pass and s2b_pass\n        s2_reason = (f\"(a) perm p_one_sided={perm['p_one_sided']:.4f} ({'pass' if s2a_pass else 'fail'}) AND \"\n                     f\"(b) direction-null: value>null_p95 on {frac_info['fraction']:.2f} of {frac_info['n']} \"\n skip_pole_mask = None\n    if cid == \"C9\" and \"c9_true_patch_pole_missing\" in gdf.columns:\n        miss = gdf[\"c9_true_patch_pole_missing\"].tolist()\n        skip_pole_mask = {pv: sign: float, gdf: pd.DataFrame, oriented_wv: np.ndarray,\n            skip_pole_mask: dict[str, np.ndarray] | None = None) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Blanket refusers must score worse than the honest instruct model sharing their lineage;\n    each honest instruct model's own wrapped poles must score worse than its own plain value.\n    skip_pole_mask: {pv: bool array over gdf} of pole entries to EXCLUDE from the check (not\n    worst-valued) -- used for C9 under ATP_UNRELIABLE when true_patch_pole_* was not measured for\n    that model (a missing measurement, not a measured-but-undefined candidate value).\"\"\"\n    idx_of_repo = {r: i for i, r in enumerate(gdf[\"repo\"].to_numpy())}\n    classes = gdf[\"class\"].to_numpy()\n    lineages = gdf[\"lineage\"].to_numpy()\n    repos = gdf[\"repo\"].to_numpy()\n\n    checks = []\n    # blanket refusers vs their lineage's honest instruct model\n    instruct_by_lineage = {lineages[i]: repos[i] for i in range(len(gdf)) if classes[i] == \"instruct\"}\n    for i in range(len(gdf)):\n        if classes[i] != \"blanket_refuser\":\n            continue\n        base_repo = instruct_by_lineage.get(lineages[i])\n        if base_repo is None:\n            continue\n        j = idx_of_repo[base_repo]\n        checks.append((\"blanket_refuser\", repos[i], base_repo, oriented_wv[i] < oriented_wv[j]))\n\n    # wrapped poles of each honest instruct model vs its own plain value\n    pole_raw = {}\n    for pv in (\"pole_refuse\", \"pole_comply\"):\n        raw, und, _ = get_raw_series(gdf, cid, pv)\n        oriented = apply_worst_value_rule(raw, und, sign)\n        pole_raw[pv] = oriented\n    lite = gdf[\"lite\"].to_numpy() if \"lite\" in gdf.columns else np.zeros(len(gdf), bool)\n    for i in range(len(gdf)):\n        if classes[i] != \"instruct\" or lite[i]:\n            continue  # ANCHOR_LITE rows never measured pole values: excluded, not worst-valued\n        for pv in (\"pole_refuse\", \"pole_comply\"):\n            if skip_pole_mask is not None and skip_pole_mask.get(pv) is not None and skip_pole_mask[pv][i]:\n                continue  # true_patch_pole_* not measured for this model: excluded, not worst-valued\n            checks.append((pv, repos[i], repos[i], pole_raw[pv][i] < oriented_wv[i]))\n\n    if not checks:\n        return {\"pass\": False, \"reason\": \"no blanket-refuser/instruct-pole pairs available in this panel\"}\n    n_ok = sum(1 for c in checks if c[3])\n    frac = n_ok / len(checks)\n    all_hold = frac == 1.0\n    detail = \"; \".join(f\"{kind}:{r} worse-than {ref}={ok}\" for kind, r, ref, ok in checks)\n    return {\"pass\": bool(all_hold), \"reason\": f\"{n_ok}/{len(checks)} ({frac:.2f}) checks hold \"\n            f\"(pass requires ALL) | {detail[:600]}\"}\n\n\n# =================================================================================================\n# Within-family\n# =================================================================================================\ndef _exact_perm_p(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, sign: float | None, max_exact: int = 8,\n                  n_mc: int = 20000) -> float:\n    \"\"\"One-sided (declared sign) or two-sided (sign None) permutation p-value of Spearman(x, y);\n    exact enumeration for n <= max_exact, else Monte-Carlo with a fixed seed.\"\"\"\n    import itertools\n    n = len(x)\n    rx = _safe_rank(np.asarray(x, float), \"wf:x\")\n    ry = _safe_rank(np.asarray(y, float), \"wf:y\")\n    obs = pearson(rx, ry)\n    if not np.isfinite(obs):\n        return float(\"nan\")\n    s = 1.0 if sign is None else float(np.sign(sign))\n    if n <= max_exact:\n        perms = np.array(list(itertools.permutations(range(n))), dtype=np.int64)\n    else:\n        rng = np.random.default_rng(SEED)\n        perms = np.array([rng.permutation(n) for _ in range(n_mc)], dtype=np.int64)\n    ryp = ry[perms]\n    rxc = rx - rx.mean()\n    rypc = ryp - ryp.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)\n    den = np.sqrt((rxc ** 2).sum() * (rypc ** 2).sum(axis=1))\n    null = np.where(den > 0, (rypc * rxc).sum(axis=1) / np.maximum(den, File: /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_fcYd_7ruOwtm/3_invention_loop/iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1/s3_bookkeeping.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""s3_bookkeeping.py -- session-3 bookkeeping (idempotent; safe to re-run after every panel stage).

1. skips.json: a repo that has a rows/<slug>.json row is MEASURED, so any skip entry for it is stale and is moved
   to skips_superseded.json (kept for provenance, with the time it was superseded).
2. DEVIATIONS.json: adds or refreshes the session-3 entries (second pod restart, hardware change, anchor quartet in
   full mode, ungraded 2-4 B extras, offset-control set) and marks the session-2 ANCHOR_QUARTET_LITE entry as
   superseded. The entry texts are regenerated from the rows on disk, so they stay true as the panel grows.
3. Coverage check: every non-sealed chat/base panel repo must appear in rows/ or in skips.json. Prints the gaps.

Usage: venv_live/bin/python s3_bookkeeping.py
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

WS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
DATA = Path("/ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_fcYd_7ruOwtm/3_invention_loop/iter_3/gen_art/gen_art_dataset_1")
ANCHORS = ["Qwen/Qwen3-4B", "Qwen/Qwen3-4B-SafeRL", "DreamFast/qwen3-4b-heretic", "mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-abliterated"]
BASE = "Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base"


def slug(repo: str) -> str:
    return repo.replace("/", "__")


def atomic_write(p: Path, obj) -> None:
    tmp = p.with_suffix(p.suffix + ".tmp")
    tmp.write_text(json.dumps(obj, indent=1))
    os.replace(tmp, p)


def load_rows() -> dict[str, dict]:
    out = {}
    for p in sorted((WS / "rows").glob("*.json")):
        r = json.loads(p.read_text())
        out[r["repo"]] = r
    return out


def flags_of(r: dict) -> set[str]:
    return {f.get("code") for f in (r.get("flags") or []) if isinstance(f, dict)}


def upsert(devs: list[dict], code: str, detail: str, affected: list[str]) -> None:
    for d in devs:
        if d.get("code") == code:
            d["detail"], d["affected_repos"] = detail, affected
            return
    devs.append({"code": code, "detail": detail, "affected_repos": affected})


def main() -> None:
    rows = load_rows()
    panel = json.loads((DATA / "panel.json").read_text())["rows"]
    prereg = json.loads((WS / "PREREG.json").read_text())
    sub = set(prereg["cpu_subpanel"])
    labels = json.loads((WS / "labels_map.json").read_text())["rows"]

    # ---- 1. skips
    skips = json.loads((WS / "skips.json").read_text()) if (WS / "skips.json").exists() else []
    sup_p = WS / "skips_superseded.json"
    superseded = json.loads(sup_p.read_text()) if sup_p.exists() else []
    keep = []
    for s in skips:
        if s["repo"] in rows:
            s2 = dict(s)
            s2["superseded_utc"] = time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime())
            s2["superseded_by"] = f"rows/{slug(s['repo'])}.json"
            if not any(x["repo"] == s["repo"] and x.get("code") == s.get("code") for x in superseded):
                superseded.append(s2)
        else:
            keep.append(s)
    atomic_write(WS / "skips.json", keep)
    atomic_write(sup_p, superseded)

    # ---- 2. deviations
    devs = json.loads((WS / "DEVIATIONS.json").read_text())
    for d in devs:
        if d.get("code") == "ANCHOR_QUARTET_LITE" and "SUPERSEDED" not in d["detail"][:40]:
            d["detail"] = ("SUPERSEDED in session 3 by ANCHOR_QUARTET_FULL_ON_CPU (no anchor row carries the ANCHOR_LITE "
                           "flag). Session-2 text kept for provenance: " + d["detail"])
        if d.get("code") == "POD_RESTART_RESUME" and "second pod restart" not in d["detail"]:
            d["detail"] += (" A second pod restart at ~17:37 UTC killed the session-2 v2 driver (run_panel_v2.sh) after 4 "
                            "of 19 v2 sub-panel rows. Session 3 (17:53 UTC) resumed from the persisted rows with "
                            "run_panel_v3.sh. The 4 rows measured on 2 threads in session 2 were moved to "
                            "scratch/rows_v2_session2_2threads/ and re-measured, so every row in rows/ was measured in "
                            "session 3 with the same code on the same 4-thread CPU allocation.")
    s3 = [r for r in rows.values()]
    anchors_measured = [a for a in ANCHORS if a in rows]
    anchors_lite = [a for a in anchors_measured if "ANCHOR_LITE" in flags_of(rows[a])]
    upsert(devs, "HARDWARE_SESSION3",
           "Session 3 ran on 4 hyperthreads = 2 physical AMD EPYC 9655P (Zen5) cores (cpuset 20,80,116,176; cgroup "
           "memory 16 GB; no GPU; no sibling agents), versus 2 hyperthreads of one core in sessions 1-2. torch uses "
           "len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) = 4 threads. All per-candidate seconds in rows/ come from this allocation; "
           "they are CPU wall-clock numbers and say nothing about S5 (GPU timing), which stays not measurable.",
           [])
    upsert(devs, "ANCHOR_QUARTET_FULL_ON_CPU",
           f"With 4 CPUs the graded Qwen3-4B anchor quartet (outside CPU_SUBPANEL) is measured in FULL mode (random-"
           f"direction nulls, k8, both wrapped poles, oracle rows, C9 true patching), with the PREREG time caps raised "
           f"to soft 2400 s / hard 3600 s (TIME_CAP_OVERRIDE flag in each row). Measured so far: "
           f"{len(anchors_measured)}/4; rows still flagged ANCHOR_LITE: {anchors_lite or 'none'}. mlabonne/Qwen3-4B-"
           f"abliterated ships fp32 shards and is loaded into bf16. Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Base (base stratum, plain "
           f"renderer, excluded from every correlation) is measured in ANCHOR_LITE mode"
           f"{' (row present)' if BASE in rows else ' (row not present yet)'}.",
           anchors_measured + ([BASE] if BASE in rows else []))
    extras = [r for r in rows if r not in sub and r not in ANCHORS and r != BASE]
    upsert(devs, "PANEL_EXTENDED_UNGRADED_EXTRAS",
           f"Session 3 also measured {len(extras)} ungraded 2-4 B chat panel rows outside CPU_SUBPANEL in full mode "
           f"(raised caps, TIME_CAP_OVERRIDE) so that iteration 5 has join-ready values for them. They have no label "
           f"and enter no correlation. Their NOT_IN_CPU_SUBPANEL skip entries moved to skips_superseded.json.",
           extras)
    upsert(devs, "OFFSET_CONTROL_SET",
           "The plan's constant-offset control set is Qwen3-4B, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, Llama-3.2-1B, TinyLlama, "
           "OLMo-2-1B and SmolLM2-360M. Session 1 substituted Qwen3-0.6B for Qwen3-4B (outside CPU_SUBPANEL). "
           "Session 3 added Qwen3-4B back (method.py OFFSET_MODELS) because the anchors now run in full mode, so "
           "the control covers 7 models: " + ", ".join(sorted(r for r in rows if rows[r].get("offset_control")))
           + ". The C9 AtP-validation set keeps its session-1 substitute (Qwen2.5-0.5B for Qwen3-4B); C9 true "
             "patching is measured on every model, so the per-model AtP-vs-true Pearson is reported for all.",
           sorted(r for r in rows if rows[r].get("offset_control")))
    atomic_write(WS / "DEVIATIONS.json", devs)

    # ---- 3. coverage
    skip_repos = {s["repo"] for s in keep}
    gaps = []
    for pr in panel:
        if pr.get("sealed") or pr.get("stratum") not in ("chat", "base"):
            continue
        if pr["repo"] not in rows and pr["repo"] not in skip_repos:
            gaps.append(pr["repo"])
    graded_rows = [r for r in rows if (labels.get(r) or {}).get("BALANCED") is not None]
    print(json.dumps({"rows": len(rows), "graded_rows": len(graded_rows), "anchors_measured": anchors_measured,
                      "extras_measured": extras, "skips_active": len(keep), "skips_superseded": len(superseded),
                      "coverage_gaps": gaps}, indent=1))
    if gaps:
        print("COVERAGE GAPS: these panel repos are neither in rows/ nor in skips.json (still queued?)", file=sys.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

k0=(N-(g.size().values**2).sum()/N)/(a-1); icc=(MSB-MSW)/(MSB+(k0-1)*MSW); neff=N/(1+(N/a-1)*icc)

onstant-offset toy: adding a constant vector c to x1 changes mean(margin) but leaves C1 and C2 unchanged to 1e-5 (linear toy).
  (d) Cross-fit test: with 16 random Gaussian 'items' of d=2048 and random labels, the in-sample diff-of-means AUROC is about 1.0 while the cross-fitted AUROC is about 0.5 +/- 0.2. This checks the fold code is not leaking.
  (e) Sealed assert: load_model('ibm-granite/granite-3.0-2b-instruct') raises before any network call.
  (f) Differing-token extraction on the 8 SCREEN16 pairs under the Qwen tokenizer returns a non-empty set for all 8. Print the tokens for manual sanity.

  === 3. PER-CHECKPOINT MEASUREMENT (live_screen.py; one process, loops checkpoints, resumable) ===
  Order: models already in the shared cache first (check with huggingface_hub.scan_cache_dir or path existence), then by ascending n_params. Download with snapshot_download(allow_patterns=['*.json','*.safetensors','tokenizer*','*.model','*.txt']). After finishing a model that was NOT in the cache at start, and only if the disk is < 25 GB free, delete ONLY that snapshot directory (never others). Record the disk state.
  For each repo:
    assert_not_sealed(repo); t0=time()
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(repo, torch_dtype=bf16, device_map='cuda', attn_implementation = 'eager' if family=='gemma2' else 'sdpa'); tok (padding_side='left'; pad = eos if missing).
    If the load fails: row status='skip', reason code in {LOAD_FAIL, TEMPLATE_MISSING, OOM, GATED, DOWNLOAD_FAIL, TIMEOUT}, then continue. EVERY skip is written to skips.json. Nothing is dropped silently.
    Layers accessed via a helper get_layers(model) covering model.model.layers (Qwen2/3, Llama, OLMo2, Gemma2, Phi3, Falcon3, SmolLM, danube(Mistral), EuroLLM(Llama)). Hooks go on decoder-layer forward outputs (output[0] is the residual stream after the layer).
    CONDITIONS = {plain, pole_refuse (always-refuse wrapper), pole_comply (never-refuse wrapper)}. Render all 16 x 3 prompts. Batch per condition (16 prompts, left-padded). The last prompt token = the last non-pad position = position -1 under left padding.
    BASE PASS (per condition, no_grad, output_hidden_states=True): store resid[l][item] at the last token for all l (float32 on CPU, 16 x L x d, about 16x36x2560x4B = 6 MB) and margin[item]. Also store the full-sequence resid at L_h and at the B_late layers for C7/C9 alignment (plain only).
    DIRECTIONS (from the plain condition only, 16 prompts):
      h_l^(k): for fold k in 4 folds (2 pairs each, fixed by pair_id order under the seed), h = mean(resid_harm) - mean(resid_twin) over the 6 training pairs, unit-normalised. You are porting an existing, reviewed CPU measurement script so it runs on an NVIDIA GPU. Do NOT change any measurement semantics.

WORKSPACE (write only here): /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_fcYd_7ruOwtm/3_invention_loop/iter_4/gen_art/gen_art_experiment_1 (called WS below).
Files you OWN and may edit: WS/method.py and WS/live_lib.py. Edit WS/tests/test_live.py only if a test needs a device fix. Do not edit any other file. NEVER write into WS/rows/, which holds finished per-model rows (it is empty now; the production run will fill it later). Never delete anything. Backups of the pre-port code already exist in WS/scratch/code_v3_cpu_pre_gpu/.

CONTEXT
method.py measures 8 causal/attention/gradient "safety metric" candidates on 16 fixed prompts per HF chat model. It runs one model at a time and uses:
- forward hooks on decoder-layer outputs;
- KV-cache reuse;
- its own greedy generation;
- a backward pass for gradient x input.
It was written for CPU (torch 2.14.0+cpu, bf16). A GPU is now available: NVIDIA L4, 23 GB.
A CUDA venv is being built at WS/venv_gpu:
- script: WS/scratch/make_venv_gpu.sh
- log: WS/logs/venv_gpu.log
- PID: WS/logs/venv_gpu.pid
Wait for it with `while kill -0 $(cat WS/logs/venv_gpu.pid) 2>/dev/null; do sleep 10; done`. Then check that `WS/venv_gpu/bin/python -c "import torch;print(torch.__version__, torch.cuda.is_available())"` prints True.
If the build failed, fix it:
- uv only, never pip.
- torch==2.14.0 CUDA wheel from https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130 (or cu128).
- Pin all other packages by WS/scratch/venv_gpu_reqs.txt.
HF cache env vars (HF_HOME etc.) are preset; never override them. Every model used below is already in the shared HF cache.

REQUIRED CHANGES (device plumbing only)
1. live_lib.py:
   - Resolve one module-level DEVICE: cuda if torch.cuda.is_available() and os.environ.get('LIVE_DEVICE','auto') != 'cpu', else cpu.
   - load_model() places the model on DEVICE. Keep attn_implementation='eager' and the given dtype.
   - build_batch() returns ids/mask/pos on DEVICE (or ModelRun.batch() moves them there).
   - Everything else stays identical.
2. Conversions:
   - Every tensor->numpy conversion (`.numpy()`) in method.py and live_lib.py must work for CUDA tensors: use `.detach().cpu().numpy()`.
   - Every numpy->torch conversion used inside forward hooks or as a model input (torch.from_numpy, torch.tensor, torch.ones, torch.full, torch.zeros, index tensors used on CUDA tensors) must be on the device of the tensor it combines with. Either `.to(h.device, h.dtype)` at use, or create it once on DEVICE outside the hook.
   - Check at least these lines, then grep for more:
     - method.py: ~325, 334, 392-401, 421-433, 454-461, 490-492, 509, 585, 622, 721, 754, 800, 997-998, 1226
     - live_lib.py: ~255-261, 338-343
3. Timing: ModelRun.tic() and toc() must call torch.cuda.synchronize() on CUDA, so per-block and per-candidate seconds measure completed GPU work. Model load time stays excluded from candidate seconds, as it is now.
4. Memory:
   - On CUDA, call torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction(9.3 / total_vram_gb) once at startup. This is the plan's 9.3 GB hard cap.
   - Call torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats() when each model starts.
   - Store torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()/1e9 in the row.
   - After each model: drop every reference to the model, gc.collect(), then torch.cuda.empty_cache() (extend ModelRun.unload()).
5. On CUDA, do NOT apply resource.setrlimit(RLIMIT_AS, ...) in main(): an address-space limit breaks CUDA initialisation. Keep it on CPU.
6. OOM fallback. The 4B models hold ~8 GB of bf16 weights, so the batched backward in grad_pass may not fit under 9.3 GB.
   - Catch torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError in grad_pass, call torch.cuda.empty_cache(), and recompute in chunks of rows, halving down to 1 item per chunk.
   - Concatenate per-item outputs so the result is identical in shape and meaning to the unchunked call. Build each chunk with b.rows(...) exactly as now, so the padded length T is unchanged.
   - Apply the same halving fallback to any other pass you actually see OOM on a 4B model.
   - Record a flag {"code":"GRAD_CHUNKED","chunk":k} in the model's flags when the fallback is used.
7. PREREG GPU-branch constants. WS/PREREG.json is hash-locked: NEVER edit it. It declares random_directions {n_cpu: 8, n_gpu: 20, used: 8} and a CPU-only budget cut C16_alphas_cpu_variants (variants use alphas [-2,0,2]).
   - On CUDA: N_RAND = PREREG['random_directions']['n_gpu'] (20), and ALPHAS_VAR = ALPHAS (all 5 alphas) for every variant.
   - On CPU: keep the current values.
   - The eps grid stays as it is (plain [0.02,0.05,0.10]; variants/nulls [0.05]).
   - These constants are computed at import time today, so resolve the device before they are set.
8. Row metadata: add row['compute'] = {'device': 'cuda'|'cpu', 'device_name', 'torch': torch.__version__, 'cuda': torch.version.cuda, 'transformers': transformers.__version__, 'dtype': 'bfloat16', 'n_rand': N_RAND, 'alphas_variants': ALPHAS_VAR, 'vram_cap_gb': 9.3 (None on CPU), 'vram_peak_gb', 'n_threads': torch.get_num_threads()}. Do not remove or rename any existing row field.
9. Nothing else changes: candidate definitions, directions, folds, seeds, layer bands, thresholds, prompts, judge calls and output schema all stay as they are (apart from the new 'compute' key and flags).

ACCEPTANCE CHECKS
Run all of them from WS with WS/venv_gpu/bin/python. Background any long run with `timeout` and a PID file, and never kill processes by name (other pipelines share this machine).
(a) `venv_gpu/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/` passes.
(b) GPU smoke on Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B:
    - Run `timeout 1500 venv_gpu/bin/python method.py --smoke --repos Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B > logs/gpu_smoke_qwen3_06b.log 2>&1`. Smoke writes WS/scratch/smoke_Qwen__Qwen3-0.6B.json, not rows/. It also makes a few OpenRouter oracle-judge calls; that costs cents and is fine.
    - Compare the plain-condition primary 'value' of every candidate in row['candidates'] (logit_gap, refusal_mass, C1, C2, C3, C7, C8, C9, C11, C16 and any others present) with the CPU row WS/scratch/rows_cpu_v3/Qwen__Qwen3-0.6B.json, which the same code produced on CPU in bf16.
    - Report a table: candidate | cpu | gpu | abs diff | rel diff.
    - Expect agreement at bf16-noise level: same sign, typically <10-15% relative, logit gap within ~0.2.
    - A sign flip, or a relative difference >30% on any candidate, must be investigated and explained or fixed before you report done. bf16 rounding differs between CPU and CUDA kernels, so small differences are expected.
(c) Anchor timing on Qwen/Qwen3-4B:
    - Run `timeout 2400 venv_gpu/bin/python method.py --smoke --repos Qwen/Qwen3-4B > logs/gpu_smoke_qwen3_4b.log 2>&1`.
    - Report: load seconds; total seconds after load; per-candidate seconds (as stored in the row); VRAM peak GB, which must be < 9.3; any flags (GRAD_CHUNKED, TIME_CAP, etc.).
    - If the total after load exceeds 120 s, just report it. Do not reduce N_RAND.
(d) Confirm that a second invocation without --smoke still skips repos whose rows/<slug>.json exists (read the code; do not create rows).

REPORT BACK, concisely:
- the changed functions and lines per file;
- the results of (a)-(d), including the comparison table and the timing/VRAM numbers;
- any blocker.
No narration and no full logs.

# Order follows the plan's fallback 7: graded checkpoints first (ascending size inside method.py's panel_order),

# rows/<slug>.json is skipped. If a stage's python process dies abnormally (not a timeout) it is re-run once.
